subtitle: An open-source business platform designed for every industry. Modular, self-hostable, international and built together by a global community.
status: Today you can register and retrieve an article by SKU in a local demo. The broader platform is a design goal, not a released ERP suite.
roadintro: Priority order, not a release calendar. Refer to the application roadmap for dependencies and acceptance criteria.
vision.intro: A small workshop and a multinational distributor both need reliable records, but their workflows differ. We want them to share business concepts without sharing a database, a cloud provider or a single prescribed way of working.
architecture.intro: Independent services own business rules, data and migrations. Published contracts let an extension integrate without writing into another service’s database.
industries.intro: One platform, many contexts. A product, lot or order can have shared identity while a future industry package supplies validated attributes, units and policies. These examples are design questions, not available packages.
community.intro: You do not need to code. Tell us what happens when a customer orders ten units and only six are available. Who decides what to ship, and what must the next shift know? Use a fictional example.
contribute.intro: Choose a small outcome and discuss it before starting. Designers can sketch the Article form; ERP practitioners can explain an exception; translators and writers can improve a confusing instruction. Developers, security reviewers and infrastructure engineers can review a contract or recovery assumption.
principle.source: Open source · inspect and adapt first-party work under Apache-2.0.
principle.community: Community-driven development · discuss requirements in public.
principle.data: Data sovereignty · keep control of business records.
principle.hosting: Self-hosting · begin with a local Compose setup.
principle.modules: Modular architecture · let each service own its rules.
principle.language: Internationalization · separate language from business identity.
principle.api: Open APIs · publish and validate service contracts.
principle.agents: Agent-native architecture · use the same authorized commands.
principle.extensions: Extensibility · integrate through interfaces, not database access.
stack.current: Current slice: Rust service, MongoDB, Docker Compose and an OpenAPI contract.
stack.target: Target: Angular browser shell, NATS JetStream for durable events, S3-compatible object storage and Model Context Protocol for approved agent tools.
stack.operations: Deployment goal: Kubernetes after migration, isolation and recovery are tested. Compose remains the local path.
industry.mechanical: Mechanical engineering · preserve the released design revision.
industry.plant: Machine and plant manufacturing · connect installed components to service history.
industry.timber: Sawmills and timber processing · relate measured volume to graded output.
industry.chemical: Chemical industries · trace lots and quality decisions.
industry.construction: Construction · track progress by site and contract.
industry.retail: Retail and wholesale · reserve and replenish stock across pack sizes.
industry.food: Food production · connect expiry dates to incoming lots.
industry.services: Professional services · deliver time and expertise without inventory.
industry.other: Other industries · bring a workflow that challenges these assumptions.
phase.foundation: Foundation: local Article slice, contracts and governance.
phase.scope: Next: verified organization and tenant scope; reliable cross-service events.
phase.order: First workflow: customer order, shortage, purchasing, receipt and reservation.
phase.preview: Before preview: test recovery, validate external integrations and document operating limits.
domain.org: Organization and tenant management; international company structures
domain.product: Product management, inventory, purchasing and sales
domain.production: Manufacturing, product structures and bills of materials
domain.trace: Recipes, material transformations, batches, serial numbers and traceability
domain.records: Digital product records, projects and quality management
domain.ai: AI and agent integration through authorized operations
